elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The inserted language covers only assignment "to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"; no affiliate carve-out appears, so an affiliate transfer falls into the "any other assignment" bucket requiring the other Party's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other Party" — Customer is covered as one of the Parties, and only notice (not consent) is required.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The new sentence is mutual: Vendor (HDI) may likewise assign to a merger/acquisition/asset-sale successor on written notice alone, so Vendor is not required to obtain Customer's consent for every assignment.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "Any other assignment of this Agreement requires the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" — applies the reasonableness standard to Customer's consent over Vendor assignments (other than successor transfers).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears anywhere in the rendered clause; Vendor could assign to a leather-goods competitor as a merger/asset-sale successor on written notice alone.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained Section 10.3 text nor the insertion creates any change-of-control trigger, and the finding records that the only termination triggers are Section 2 non-renewal/notice and the Section 1 delivery-failure right, so no Vendor CoC termination right exists to delete.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" — expressly mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Successor assignment is permitted "upon written notice to the other Party."

"Any other assignment of this Agreement requires the prior written consent of the other Party." The retained Section 10.3 text is pure binding-effect/successors-and-assigns language and contains no no-consent exception (no affiliate or other carve-out) that would defeat this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld."

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: a mutual successor-assignment right, a written-notice condition, a consent requirement for all other assignments, and a not-unreasonably-withheld standard all appear in the two inserted sentences.
Preferred is not reached (no affiliate carve-out, no asymmetric Vendor consent requirement, no competitor bar), but the drafter expressly targeted the fallback, so the redline is position-complete.

Minimality holds: the original Section 10.3 binding-effect sentence is retained verbatim with no deletions or paraphrase, and the insertion adds nothing outside the fallback checklist — no survival tail, no change-of-control mechanic, no notice-period or expense boilerplate, and no notwithstanding-style override of the existing clause.

Intent is preserved: the added sentences are a self-contained assignment mechanic that does not contradict the retained "binding upon ... successors and assigns" language, introduces no undefined term, and creates no dangling cross-reference; unrelated termination, renewal and delivery mechanics are untouched.

No repair is required for the claimed fallback level. If the team later wants the preferred position, the operative additions needed are (i) "Customer may assign to any Affiliate without the other Party's consent," (ii) removal of "Either Party" in favour of a Customer-only successor right so that every Vendor assignment needs Customer consent, and (iii) an express bar on Vendor assigning to a competitor of Customer.
